text:
Olivia: FYI hit an angry morning where multiple tenants triggered scale and clusters spiked. Thinking we need a controller-side admission score instead of pure rate-limits.
Amir: +1. Rate-limits felt too rigid last time. Admission score could combine operator backlog, tenant weight, recent failures.
Zoe: what data points do we have for backlog? operator.apply_queue_len and last_apply_duration per shard?
Karthik: we emit operator.apply_queue_len but it's coarse. we can add per-tenant apply_counts and a moving avg of apply_latency.
Priya: ops perspective: whatever we add must be auditable (why a tenant was denied fast-path). need a short reason in traces.
Olivia: rough scoring: score = w1*operator_backlog_norm + w2*(1 - tenant_credit_norm) + w3*recent_errors - w4*tenant_priority. Lower score -> deny fast path.
Amir: don't forget region capacity signals. a tenant in eu-west shouldn't be penalized by us-east spikes if they have dedicated pools. maybe normalize per-pool.
Zoe: also trend detection: if desired_delta is growing exponentially, prefer smoothing. simple leaky bucket on the desired_delta timeline could prevent spikes.
Karthik: implementation plan: (1) compute signals in controller cache (2) scoring function (pluggable) (3) short-circuit fast-path if score>threshold (4) emit decision event with reason and metrics.
Priya: for rollouts, we need a canary with a synthetic tenant that issues controlled bursts. simulate operator slowness too.
Olivia: test harness idea: replay historical intent spikes against the new admission logic and measure overshoot vs latency. we have traces from 2024-11-12 incident that are perfect.
Amir: edge cases: what if operator is healthy but cloud node provisioning is thrashed (cloud-side limits)? score will look fine. need external cloud-limited flag from operator.
Zoe: agree. operator should surface a boolean 'cloud_rate_limited' and available_node_estimate. incorporate into score.
Karthik: also metrics: admission_denied_count, avg_score_per_tenant, fastpath_accepted_percent. tie alerts when denied_count > 0.5% of requests.
Priya: add human-friendly reasons: "backlog", "low_credits", "global_headroom_exhausted", "cloud_limit" and surface in tenant dashboard.
Olivia: about global headroom: lean toward a small emergency buffer that refills slowly, funded by tokens from low-usage tenants (redistribution). but must be transparent in billing.
Amir: can we implement a borrowing mechanism: if tenant A borrows global_headroom, tag costs to A and optionally charge a premium. ops wants this for cost control.
Zoe: Bonus: expose a debug endpoint that returns the score calculation for a tenant id so SREs can triage.
Karthik: pseudo config for scoring: 
```
scoring:
  backlog_weight: 0.5
  credits_weight: 0.3
  error_weight: 0.2
  priority_bonus: 0.4
  deny_threshold: 0.7
  hysteresis_windows: 3
```
Amir: add hysteresis: require X consecutive windows to flip decision, and a cooldown of Y seconds after flip.
Priya: playbook: if many tenants denied -> run automatic emergency-borrow with opt-in for high-SLA tenants and page infra if global_headroom < 10% for 5m.
Olivia: rollout: prototype in controller branch, unit tests + replay harness, canary to 3 clusters, monitor overshoot/queue-length/latency, then 25% rollout.
Karthik: storage: we should persist per-tenant token state in controller leader cache (in-memory with snapshot) not in k8s etcd. must survive leader failover with snapshot replication.
Zoe: small UX ask: annotate scaling actions with admission_reason in the event stream so auditors can group decisions.
Amir: CI bot: ran quick simulation against 2024-11-12 trace: baseline overshoot 4.8x -> with admission score reduced to 1.2x. attaching results in RFC.
Priya: nice. also confirm how this interacts with warmup credits and dedicated pool reservations. we should prefer consuming warmup credits before denying.
Olivia: noted. I'll draft the RFC with scoring formula, config knobs, telemetry, and rollout plan. will include replay results. assigning myself to draft and Karthik to prototype cache.
Karthik: will start prototype tomorrow, will add debug endpoint and decision events.
Zoe: I'll wire dashboards and alerts.
Amir: I'll help tune weights and provide simulation harness.
Priya: ops will validate playbook and billing annotations.
ci-bot: build status: controller-proto branch passed unit + integration tests (12/14).
Olivia: thanks folks. I'll post RFC link here in ~24h. :sparkles:
